title: Home Mortgage Loans: Refund of the Escrow Balance After Payoff
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Refund of the Escrow Balance After Payoff

Once a loan under Home Mortgage Loans has been paid in full, any money left in its escrow balance belongs back with the borrower. This page sets the deadline for that refund and the way the days toward it are counted.

## Clause

The escrow balance remaining after a payoff is refunded no later than the end of the program's post-payoff refund period, counted in calendar days from the payoff.

## Counting the deadline

- **Anchor.** The payoff date is the date the bank's records show the loan as closed by payoff.
- **Day 1.** The first calendar day after that payoff date is day 1.
- **Deadline.** The refund is due by the payoff date advanced by the number of days in the program's refund period. A refund made on that final day is within the deadline; the final day is included.
- **Which loan.** The dates used are those of the loan that was paid off.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical refund period of 20 days)

The period length and dates are invented to show the counting; each program publishes its own period.

| Payoff date | Final day of the period | Refund made on | Within the deadline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 August | 25 August | 18 August | yes |
| 5 August | 25 August | 25 August | yes, the final day counts |
| 5 August | 25 August | 26 August | no, one day late |

## Basis questions

**Does the refund period start on the day of payoff?** No. The payoff date itself is day zero; counting begins with the next calendar day.

**Are weekends skipped?** No. The period is measured in calendar days.
